results.content:
Title: Data versioning and reproducible ML with DVC and MLflow | Adaltas
# Data versioning and reproducible ML with DVC and MLflow. Never miss our publications about Open Source, big data and distributed systems, low frequency of one email every two months. Our talk on data versioning and reproducible Machine Learning proposed to the Data + AI Summit (formerly known as Spark+AI) is accepted. Registration is now open, register and join our talk. The discussion is build upon two previous articles on how to use DVC for data versioning and how to reproduce Data Science experiments with MLflow. Below is our submited proposal. Machine Learning development involves comparing models and storing the artifacts they produced. We assess different hyper-parameters to fine-tune the model. Git helps us store multiple versions of our code. Additionally, we need to keep track of the datasets we are using. This is important not only for audit purposes but also for assessing the performances of the models, developed at a later time. Git is a standard code versioning tool in software development. It can be used to store your datasets but it does not offer an optimal solution. An alternative solution is to use Data Version Control (DVC). Despite its name, it is not just a data versioning tool, but also enables model and pipeline tracking. It runs on top of Git, which makes it easy to learn for Git users. At the same time, it overcomes the limitations of storing big files by storing them remotely (e.g. Azure, S3) and keeping in Git only their metadata. MLflow is a tool that is easily integrated with the code of your model and can track dependencies, model parameters, metrics, and artifacts. Every run is linked with its corresponding Git commit. Once the model is trained, MLflow can pack it in different flavors (e.g. Python/R function, H2O, Spark, TensorFlow…) ready to be deployed. DVC also runs along with Git. When MLflow helps you manage Machine Learning lifecycle, DVC helps you manage your datasets. In this tutorial, we will learn how to leverage the capabilities of these powerful tools. We will go through a toy ML project and look at the sample code on how to increase the reproducibility of individual steps.

results.title: Best Practices for Integrated DVC/MLflow
results.content:
Title: Best Practices for Integrated DVC/MLflow
Integrating Data Version Control (DVC) and MLflow Tracking creates a powerful combination for managing machine learning projects. Recommendations for effectively using DVC and MLflow together are consolidated. │ ├── raw/ # Raw, immutable data (potentially DVC-tracked). │ ├── processed/ # Processed data (output of DVC stages). │ └── features/ # Feature data (output of DVC stages). ├── models/ # Trained models (potentially DVC-tracked). ├── src/ # Source code for data processing, training, etc. ├── .dvcignore # Specify files/directories DVC should ignore. ├── dvc.yaml # DVC pipeline definitions. Reproducibility depends on knowing the exact state of your code, data, configuration, and environment for any given experiment run. `git add src/train_model.py params.yaml dvc.lock data/.dvc`. Each Git commit should represent a coherent change, linking the code version, the data versions (via `.dvc` files and `dvc.lock`), and the configuration (`params.yaml`) used. MLflow automatically logs the Git commit hash associated with a run, creating a link back to this snapshot. ### Explicitly Link DVC Data Versions to MLflow Runs. While MLflow logs the Git commit, which indirectly points to DVC-tracked data via `.dvc` files, explicitly logging data version information in MLflow adds clarity. data_version = dvc.api.read('data/processed/features.csv.dvc') # Reads the .dvc file content. # Or get the hash of the directory itself if using newer DVC versions. # data_status = dvc.api.status(['data/processed'], show_checksum=True). # Log the DVC hash (example, needs parsing from dvc.api.read output). # mlflow.log_param("dvc_data_md5", data_version['outs'][0]['md5']). mlflow.log_param("dvc_input_data", "data/processed/features.csv") # Log path. Define your workflow steps (data processing, feature engineering, training) as stages in `dvc.yaml` rather than relying solely on individual scripts or notebooks run manually. Integrate MLflow logging directly into the commands executed by DVC stages:. cmd: python src/process_data.py --config=params.yaml. cmd: python src/train_model.py --config=params.yaml. - metrics.json: # DVC can track metrics from files. - models/model.pkl # Track the final model with DVC`. Your `src/train_model.py` script would contain the necessary `mlflow.start_run()`, `mlflow.log_param()`, `mlflow.log_metric()`, and `mlflow.log_artifact()` calls. Use a configuration file like `params.yaml` (tracked by Git) to store hyperparameters, file paths, and other settings. This keeps configuration consistent across DVC pipeline definitions, script execution, and MLflow tracking. By adhering to these practices, you create a system where DVC manages your data lifecycle and pipeline execution, while MLflow provides detailed records of your experiments.

results.title: Day 66: Data Versioning and Management — DVC, MLflow | by Adithya Prasad Pandelu | Medium
results.content:
Title: Day 66: Data Versioning and Management — DVC, MLflow | by Adithya Prasad Pandelu | Medium
# Day 66: Data Versioning and Management — DVC, MLflow. Similarly, in machine learning projects, keeping track of data, code, and model versions is crucial for **reproducibility**, **collaboration**, and **efficient experimentation**. This is where **data versioning and management** tools like **DVC (Data Version Control)** and **MLflow** come into play. In this article, we’ll explore what data versioning is, why it’s essential, and how DVC and MLflow can simplify managing machine learning projects. ## What is Data Versioning? Data versioning is the process of tracking changes to datasets and models over time. Just as software version control systems like **Git** track code changes, data versioning tools ensure that datasets, preprocessed data, and trained models are tied to specific experiments or project iterations. ## Why is Data Versioning Important? 3. **Auditability**: Track the lineage of data and models to understand how they evolved. 4. **Experiment Management**: Easily compare results from different versions of data and models. ## Challenges in Managing Data and Models. * **Size of Data**: Large datasets make it impractical to store multiple versions on local machines. ## Introducing DVC (Data Version Control). DVC is a lightweight, Git-compatible tool designed for managing data, code, and models in machine learning projects. 1. **Data and Model Versioning**: Tracks changes to datasets and model files, even for large files. DVC links each data version to a specific commit in Git, ensuring reproducibility. Save and version your model in the MLflow Model Registry:. **Use DVC** when your project involves large datasets and you need versioning and reproducibility. **Use MLflow** when you want to manage and deploy models while tracking experiments. You can combine DVC and MLflow to create a robust ML pipeline. Version Your Data with DVC**:. * Use DVC to track and version raw and processed datasets. * Log metrics, hyperparameters, and model versions with MLflow. * Use MLflow’s model registry and serving capabilities to deploy models trained on DVC-managed datasets. Data versioning and management are indispensable in machine learning projects. Tools like **DVC** and **MLflow** streamline these processes, enabling teams to work collaboratively, reproducibly, and efficiently. Whether you’re tracking datasets or deploying models, integrating these tools into your workflow can significantly improve project management and scalability.

results.title: DVC and MLFlow - reproduce experiments using git commit ids - Questions - Community Forum | Data Version Control · DVC
results.content: # DVC and MLFlow - reproduce experiments using git commit ids. I’ve started using DVC and I love it, thank you for your work! I have a question regarding DVC and MLFlow combination. I am using DVC to build/run pipelines and version data and models. And I am using MLFlow to have a nice overview of all the experiments and to visualize/store metrics and plots of the experiments. During the training and evaluation stages, I am logging stuff to MLFlow (including current git commit id for reproducibility). Let’s say I checked my MLFlow dashboard and I want to get the trained model of the last run. It is linked to the commit A. And I can’t log commit B to the MLFlow run during training/evaluation because I haven’t created commit B yet. So after `dvc repro` is done and I commit my results, I can run a short script that will add the current commit id (commit B) to the right MLFlow run (**mlflow\_run\_id**).
